item.title: Former Council Candidate Criticises Campaign Group Over Maternity Services Debate
item.description: A former council candidate has criticised the Caithness Health Action Team over its handling of the maternity services debate, following figures showing just six births at Caithness General Hospital in 2025.The post Former Council Candidate Criticises Campaign Group Over Maternity Services Debate appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: Concerns Raised Over Chronic Pain Treatment Changes at NHS Highland
item.description: Concerns have been raised over NHS Highland’s decision to stop offering injections and interventional treatments to new chronic pain patients, with questions now being asked about whether the move came years before a national review was completed.The post Concerns Raised Over Chronic Pain Treatment Changes at NHS Highland appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: Young Scots Have Saved Hundreds as Free Bus Travel Continues in Scotland
item.description: New analysis shows young people in Scotland have saved hundreds of pounds through free bus travel, as rising fares in England leave many under 22s paying more than £1,000 a year following the UK government’s decision not to introduce a similar scheme.The post Young Scots Have Saved Hundreds as Free Bus Travel Continues in Scotland appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: Garden Waste Permits Now Available for Moray Residents
item.description: Moray residents are being encouraged to order their 2026 garden waste permits by 6 March to ensure delivery ahead of the new collection year, with permits required for brown bins containing garden waste from 1 April.The post Garden Waste Permits Now Available for Moray Residents appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: Shetland Residents Invited to Take Part in Climate Conversation Survey
item.description: Shetland residents are being invited to share their views on climate change as the Shetland Climate Conversation Survey returns for 2026, giving the community a chance to shape future priorities and projects across the islands.The post Shetland Residents Invited to Take Part in Climate Conversation Survey appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: Rachel Groves Wins BBC Radio Scotland Young Traditional Musician 2026
item.description: Lever harp player Rachel Groves has been crowned BBC Radio Scotland Young Traditional Musician 2026 after a live final at Glasgow’s City Halls, celebrating the strength and diversity of Scotland’s next generation of traditional music talent.The post Rachel Groves Wins BBC Radio Scotland Young Traditional Musician 2026 appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: Raise a Glass to Exclusive Sea and Spirit Experience on Argyll Coast
item.description: An exclusive Sea and Spirit dining experience will take place at the Pierhouse Hotel in Port Appin on 27 March, pairing a six course Argyll seafood tasting menu with Oban whisky to celebrate a new coastal partnership.The post Raise a Glass to Exclusive Sea and Spirit Experience on Argyll Coast appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: A Flexible Space at The Edge of The Map in Durness
item.description: Set at the entrance to the Balnakeil Craft Village near Durness, this flexible unit offers scope for commercial use or residential conversion, with generous space, outdoor ground, and a rare position within one of the Highlands’ most distinctive coastal settings.The post A Flexible Space at The Edge of The Map in Durness appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: £90 Million Investment Set Out to Tackle Economic Inactivity
item.description: A £90 million investment has been outlined in the Scottish Government’s draft Budget to tackle economic inactivity, support parents and disabled people into work, and help reduce child poverty through expanded employability and training programmes.The post £90 Million Investment Set Out to Tackle Economic Inactivity appeared first on The Highland Times.

item.title: Fort William Mountain Festival Returns This Month With Packed 2026 Programme
item.description: The Fort William Mountain Festival returns from 12 to 15 February 2026, bringing four days of adventure, film, workshops and mountain culture to Fort William and Lochaber as one of the UK’s leading outdoor festivals gets underway.The post Fort William Mountain Festival Returns This Month With Packed 2026 Programme appeared first on The Highland Times.
